text:
Noah Laba is 22 games into his second season with the Rangers and still looking for his first goal. The New York Post wrote that he's "focusing on the positives of goalless Rangers campaign," and there are some to focus on. He has six assists, four of them in his last 10 games, and three expected goals, so he keeps getting the looks. Goals tend to follow chances.

The harder part is the five-on-five picture. New York takes just 43% of the shot attempts and 44% of the expected goals with him on the ice, nearly 12 points worse than without him. His chance rate has slipped from last season too (0.55 expected goals per 60, down from 0.75). He has been lucky on the other end: the Rangers have scored 3.1 more goals than their chances with him out there.

His value has never been mainly offense. Evolving-Hockey had most of his 0.7 wins above replacement last season coming from the penalty kill, and he's quick (89th percentile top speed). The 2022 fourth-round pick has a role; the question beyond the first goal is whether the five-on-five numbers improve.
